gold_trend_state.label: Last stand
gold_trend_state.why: Price is at the long-term make-or-break line - the last place buyers of the whole trend historically defend. BUYING works only if this line visibly holds; watch the reaction, not the touch. SELLING here locks in ahead of a potential full breakdown; many investors give it exactly one bounce attempt to decide.
gold_trend_state.tech: price $4467 is sitting right at its 200-day average ($4502, 0.8% away) - the long-term boundary where the whole uptrend historically gets defended or lost; every shorter average (50-day $4186, 100-day $4415) is already above the price.

silver_trend_state.label: Trend broken
silver_trend_state.why: The long-term line is lost. BUYING now is fighting the tide - "cheap" can get much cheaper, and most big losses happen below this line. Standing aside or SELLING protects capital; the disciplined re-entry is only after price retakes the line and holds it, even if that means paying more later.
silver_trend_state.tech: price $65.51 has closed below its 200-day average ($70.71) by 7.4% - the long-term trend line is lost, and the shorter averages (50-day $62.39, 100-day $69.28) now sit overhead as resistance rather than support.

The year itself is expected to deliver about +11.6% earnings growth ($13.43 vs $12.03 last year), then +7.4% more in FY27, with 8.6%/yr expected over 3-5 years. The stock is not cheap for it (Forward PE 22.6, PEG 2.64, Value grade D) - you are paying a full price for a high-quality compounder, which is why Zacks rates it 2-Buy rather than Strong Buy. Last quarter fits the pattern: earnings beat on volume growth even as sales missed - margins and execution carrying the story. For your 832 shares the practical read for the coming months: hold through the November report with the surprise setup in your favor, expect the $1.81/quarter dividend (~$1,506 gross / ~$1,054 net to you) to keep arriving, and watch whether the revision wave continues - that, more than the price, is the signal these analysts are following.

gold.label: Gold
gold.nature: Monetary metal — industrial use is only about 5% of demand, so gold is priced almost entirely by macro.

favouring.label: CPI inflation
favouring.why: Metals are bought as an inflation hedge. CPI at 3.4% sits well above the 2% target, which supports that case.

favouring.label: Gold speculative positioning
favouring.why: Futures net length is 53.2% of open interest, +5.9 points on the week. Positioning does not cause the move; it shows how crowded the trade already is. Heavy length means a thin cushion, washed-out length means room to run.

pressuring.label: 10-year REAL yield
pressuring.why: Precious metals pay no income, so the real yield IS the cost of holding them. At 2.45% real (10Y 4.72% minus 2.27% breakeven inflation) that cost is high.

pressuring.label: US dollar (DXY)
pressuring.why: Metals are priced in dollars, so a firmer dollar mechanically pressures them. DXY 99.96, up on the week, up versus its moving averages.

pressuring.label: Gold price trend
pressuring.why: Price is down its moving averages with RSI 69.1. Trend confirms a move, it does not cause one.

neutral.label: Fed policy rate
neutral.why: Cash competes with metal. A 3.75% policy rate is a moderate hurdle for a non-yielding asset.
